_comment: SecurityInsight's DEPLOY CONTRACT. Ships WITH the solution (operator decision 2026-08-07) so changing how SI deploys never requires editing ~30 per-customer manifests. The customer's local Sync-AutomateIT.json says WHETHER they take SI and which OPTIONAL capabilities they want; the central promotion map says WHICH VERSION and which capabilities are approved for their ring; this file says HOW. Three owners, three files, no overlap.
_needsSchema_comment: FALSE, and verified rather than assumed: analyzer-web/ contains no DbContext, no Migrations, no SqlConnection and no EntityFramework reference. SIA's only durable state is the two Azure Tables from audit #7/#9, and the APP creates them itself at startup (src/SIAnalyzer.Web/Program.cs:97 and :136, table.CreateIfNotExists()). Table storage is schemaless and additive, so there is nothing to migrate. The SQL/schema half of the platform update design is PIM's problem, not a shared one.
_capabilities_comment: What KINDS of change an SI update performs. 'optional' means a customer may switch it off in their local manifest; a required capability cannot be blocked (the block is refused and reported, so nobody can brick their own install).

capabilities.name: code
capabilities.description: The PowerShell engines and their rule/report catalogs -- plain file copy. This IS SecurityInsight; without it there is no solution.

capabilities.name: container
capabilities.description: Builds and rolls the SIA container image. Requires an Azure Container Registry and a Container Apps environment in the customer's own tenant.

capabilities.name: web-frontend
capabilities.description: The SI Analyzer (SIA) web UI: revision roll, managed-identity grants and Easy Auth. SIA is an EXTENSION of SecurityInsight, not the main program -- the engines run and produce full output with this switched off, so 'SI engine-only' is a supported topology, not a degraded one.

_deploy_comment: Entry point for the capabilities above. Health-gates itself: PROD warms a new revision and REFUSES to shift traffic unless /health returns 200, keeps the previous revision provisioned for instant rollback, and re-checks health after the swap. Grant/auth steps are idempotent, so a daily re-run is safe.

deploy._auth_comment: The script signs the az CLI in itself via auth/Connect-SIAzCli.ps1 (audit #33): MI -> Az PowerShell -> the SPN secret from THAT customer's AutomateIT Key Vault -> az login. An Az PowerShell context is NOT an az CLI context, so this cannot be inherited from the caller.

_requires_comment: Provisioning preconditions for the OPTIONAL capabilities only. A customer who blocks both needs none of these -- which is the point of making them blockable.
